Repositories

Repositories lists the packages available in the Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10 content repositories.

Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10 provides software through several content repositories including BaseOS, AppStream, CodeReady Linux Builder, Supplementary, Extensions, and High Availability repositories. The package listings include the package name, license, application compatibility level, and RHEL 10 minor release version.

  • The BaseOS repository
    The BaseOS repository provides core OS functionality for all installations. This content is available in the RPM format and is subject to support terms similar to those in previous Red Hat Enterprise Linux releases. For more information, see the Scope of Coverage Details document.
  • The AppStream repository
    Content in the AppStream repository includes additional user space applications, runtime languages, and databases in support of the varied workloads and use cases.
  • The CodeReady Linux Builder repository
    The CodeReady Linux Builder repository provides additional developer packages. It is included with all Red Hat Enterprise Linux subscriptions but need not be enabled on runtime deployments. Its packages are unsupported. For more information, see How to enable CodeReady Linux Builder.
  • The Supplementary repository
    The Supplementary repository contains proprietary packages absent from Red Hat Enterprise Linux open source repositories. Red Hat does not support them, or guarantee their ABIs. For more information, see the Support policy of the optional and supplementary channels in Red Hat Enterprise Linux.
  • The Extensions repository
    The Extensions repository will contain hand-picked upstream content that has gone through Red Hat’s Secure Supply Chain to ensure trust in its chain of custody.
  • The High Availability add-on
    The High Availability add-on provides on-demand failover services between nodes within a cluster. The add-on is available with a separate subscription. For details, see the Support Policies for RHEL High Availability Clusters.
